features.feature_value: Focused on threats/harassment/hate/violence and tone/content rather than agreeing/disagreeing with the political viewpoint.
features.evidence_span: focused more on the tone and content of the posts than on the political viewpoint being expressed
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states they used a content/tone safety standard rather than political agreement.

features.feature_value: Using both versions helped them apply the same standard consistently across political perspectives, though it didn’t strongly change decisions.
features.evidence_span: Seeing both versions side by side helped me check for consistency and apply the same standard
features.rationale: They attribute limited influence to a consistency-check benefit from seeing both versions.

features.feature_value: Removed items with offensive language and claimed they were not biased.
features.evidence_span: remove the ones with offensive language. I don’t think I was being biased at all
features.rationale: They describe their removal target and explicitly deny bias.

features.feature_value: Would tolerate vitriol/profanity if not personal attacks; rejected only when personal attacks occurred.
features.evidence_span: I don't mind some vitriol and profanity... I only rejected ones that made personal attacks
features.rationale: They define a specific conditional rule for acceptance vs rejection.

features.feature_value: Reacted to extreme statements as sad/anger-inducing and suspected rage bait while believing people may hold those views; low influence overall.
features.evidence_span: The statements were extreme... It is very sad... It seemed like rage bait
features.rationale: Their reflection centers on emotional reaction (sad/extreme) and a suspicion about intent.

features.feature_value: Allowed posts as long as there wasn’t vulgar language or threats.
features.evidence_span: As long as there wasn't vulgar language or threats I allowed it.
features.rationale: They provide a clear acceptance threshold tied to vulgarity/threats.

features.feature_value: Supports free speech and opposes censorship except when language incites violence; acknowledges disagreement with appropriateness of language.
features.evidence_span: I believe in free speech... I don't believe in censorship unless it is actually inciting people to violence
features.rationale: They use a free-speech-with-incitement-exception rule that limits removal.
